evals.prompt: Generate a typewriter hero that types 'Shipping', cycles through 'faster releases, cleaner diffs, calmer reviews', and stops on the last phrase instead of looping.
evals.expected_output: A single self-contained HTML file generated via --mode typewriter with --no-loop, cycling the three phrases and settling on 'calmer reviews'.
expectations: The generator is invoked with --mode typewriter and --no-loop
The output HTML contains const LOOP = false
The output passes validate_conductor_motion.py with 0 errors
The rotator words in the output match the three requested phrases
The output contains a prefers-reduced-motion media query

evals.prompt: I need an AI-assistant demo panel: user asks a question, the answer streams in like a real model response, with a stop button.
evals.expected_output: streaming-text mode output with chunk-buffered streaming, scroll anchoring, a stop/regenerate button, and a polite aria-live completion announcement.
expectations: The streaming-text mode/template is used
The output contains overflow-anchor: none on the streaming message
The output contains aria-live="polite" and does not use aria-live="assertive"
Streaming flushes at word boundaries rather than per character
The output passes validate_conductor_motion.py with 0 errors

evals.prompt: Give me a demo of animated popovers, a confirmation dialog, and toasts that slide in — pure CSS transitions where possible.
evals.expected_output: top-layer mode output where popover and dialog entry/exit are driven by @starting-style + transition-behavior: allow-discrete + overlay, with JS only for showModal/close and toast lifetimes.
expectations: The output contains @starting-style rules
The output transitions list both overlay and display with allow-discrete
The dialog ::backdrop is animated via background-color, not backdrop-filter
Toast lifetimes freeze while document.hidden and resume on return
The output passes validate_conductor_motion.py with 0 errors

evals.prompt: Generate the progress simulation but slower — 9 seconds total, starting at 12 percent, with quart easing.
evals.expected_output: progress mode output where --progress-duration 9000, --start-percent 12, and --easing quart each demonstrably change the generated file.
expectations: TOTAL_MS = 9000 appears in the output
START_PROGRESS = 12 appears in the output
The ease alias is swapped to a quart function (Math.pow(1 - t, 4))
The generated file differs from a default-flags generation of the same mode
The progress fill animates transform: scaleX, never .style.width, and aria-valuenow updates each tick

evals.prompt: Build a scroll-triggered section reveal for a long marketing page — modern browsers first, older ones still covered.
evals.expected_output: Reveals driven by CSS animation-timeline: view() inside @supports as the primary path, with IntersectionObserver attached only when CSS.supports reports no animation-timeline support, and @starting-style (not double-rAF) for the load-time cascade.
expectations: The output contains animation-timeline: view() inside an @supports block
IntersectionObserver attachment is gated on !CSS.supports('animation-timeline: view()')
The scroll-driven animation uses animation-fill-mode backwards, not both
The load-time hero cascade uses @starting-style or documents double-rAF as the legacy fallback
Content is visible with JavaScript disabled
